sources.entry: Anchr - Toolbox for tiny tasks on the internet, including bookmark collections, URL shortening and (encrypted) image uploads. (Source Code) GPL-3.0 Nodejs

summary.what_it_does: Anchr provides searchable bookmark collections, organized into categories, where each saved link can have an optional description. It offers a link shortener that checks new shortlinks against Google's Safe Browsing API when a key is configured. It supports image uploads where users can encrypt images client-side with a password using CryptoJS. The README also lists OAuth 2 login (Google, Facebook), Prometheus metrics, ShareX integration, and a Telegram bot. The backend runs on Node.js with MongoDB (or FerretDB), and it can be run natively or via docker-compose.
use_cases: save web links for later across devices
shorten long URLs with query parameters or tokens
self-host a personal link and image hosting service
how_to_run: git clone the repository and copy .env.example to .env, then set required variables such as ANCHR_DB_PASSWORD and ANCHR_SECRET
Run natively with 'yarn start' and 'yarn start:frontend' for development, or 'yarn run build' then 'yarn run production'; alternatively run 'docker-compose up' after sourcing env.sh
notable: Client-side password encryption of uploaded images using CryptoJS
Shortlinks checked against Google Safe Browsing API
Official Android app and Chrome/Firefox browser extensions mentioned
Hosted GDPR-compliant instance at Anchr.io alongside self-hosting
caveats: Project is considered mostly feature-complete with only occasional dependency updates
Parts use older ES5 JavaScript and Grunt/Bower tooling, though backend was recently refactored to modern syntax
Requires Node.js 21+ and MongoDB 6+ (or FerretDB) plus several environment variables to configure
